The '''2015–16 Serie A''' (known as the [[Serie A]] [[Telecom Italia Mobile|TIM]] for sponsorship reasons) was the 114th season of top-tier Italian [[association football|football]], the 84th in a [[round-robin tournament]], and the 6th since its organization under a league committee separate from [[Serie B]]. [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] were the defending champions. The campaign began on 22 August 2015 and ended on 15 May 2016.

On 25 April 2016, Juventus succeeded in defending their title for the fifth consecutive season, after second placed [[S.S.C. Napoli|Napoli]] lost to [[A.S. Roma|Roma]], giving [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] a 12-point lead with only three games left.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/juventus/story/2858561/juventus-win-fifth-straight-serie-a-title-after-napoli-lose-to-roma|title=Juventus win fifth straight Serie A title after Napoli lose to Roma|publisher=ESPN FC|date=25 April 2016|access-date=25 April 2016}}</ref>

==Events==

On 28 April 2015 [[Carpi F.C. 1909|Carpi]] obtained its first promotion ever to [[Serie A]], after debuting in [[Serie B]] the year before, becoming the 64th team to participate in Serie A since the [[1929–30 Serie A|1929–30 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/apr/29/italian-club-carpi-extraordinary-serie-a-promotion |title=Italian club Carpi celebrate clinching 'extraordinary' Serie A promotion &#124; Football |work=The Guardian |date=29 April 2015 |access-date=16 October 2015}}</ref> On 16 May, [[Frosinone Calcio|Frosinone]] also earned its first promotion to Serie A, becoming the 65th to participate.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/10/italy/2015/05/16/11803592/frosinone-secure-historic-serie-a-promotion |title=Frosinone promoted to Serie A for first time |publisher=Goal |date=16 May 2015 |access-date=16 October 2015}}</ref> On 9 June 2015 [[Bologna F.C. 1909|Bologna]] won [[2014–15 Serie B#Promotion playoffs|Serie B play-off]], returning to the Serie A after just one year.

This season of Serie A was the first season to have [[goal-line technology]] implemented after severe complaints from various teams' general managers (first [[Adriano Galliani]]) in relation to controversial [[ghost goal]]s during recent seasons of Serie A.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.co.uk/italian-serie-a/story/2297461/serie-a-approves-goal-line-technology-for-next-season |title=Serie A approves goal-line technology for next season |publisher=ESPN FC |date=13 February 2015 |access-date=16 October 2015}}</ref>

On 20 March 2016, [[Gianluigi Buffon]] broke the previous record of [[Sebastiano Rossi]] (929 minutes) by setting a longer period of 974 minutes without conceding a goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legaseriea.it/it/sala-stampa/notizie/info/record-di-imbattibilita-per-buffon-974|title=RECORD DI IMBATTIBILITA' PER BUFFON: 974' - News - Lega Serie A|access-date=16 May 2016|archive-date=2 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170802205651/http://www.legaseriea.it/it/sala-stampa/notizie/info/record-di-imbattibilita-per-buffon-974|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 14 May, [[Gonzalo Higuaín]] broke [[Gunnar Nordahl]]'s record for most goals scored in Serie A (20 teams championship) in a season (35 in [[1949–50 Serie A|1949–50]]) and equaled [[Gino Rossetti]]'s record in [[1928–29 Divisione Nazionale|1928–29]] (that was composed of 32 teams, instead) by scoring 36 goals and winning the [[Capocannoniere]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/84347/higuain-i-am-so-happy|title=Higuain: 'I am so happy!'|publisher=Football Italia|date=14 May 2016|access-date=14 May 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/723/serie-a/2016/05/14/23529832/higuain-makes-serie-a-history-by-breaking-66-year-old|title=Higuain makes Serie A history by breaking 66-year-old goalscoring record|publisher=Goal|author=Chris Davie|date=14 May 2016|access-date=14 May 2016}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legaseriea.it/it/sala-stampa/notizie/info/higuain-nella-storia-del-calcio-italiano|title=HIGUAIN NELLA STORIA DEL CALCIO ITALIANO - News - Lega Serie A|access-date=16 May 2016|archive-date=4 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161004150527/http://www.legaseriea.it/it/sala-stampa/notizie/info/higuain-nella-storia-del-calcio-italiano|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Three Serie A icons also retired at the end of the season; the [[Hellas Verona F.C.|Verona]] captain [[Luca Toni]], who scored 157 goals in 324 league appearances and was twice the league's top scorer, as well as [[Gianpaolo Bellini]], the [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left-back]] who spent his entire career with [[Atalanta B.C.|Atalanta]], making 435 appearances with the club. Both players also scored in their final games with their clubs on 8 May 2016, Toni in a 2–1 win over champions [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] and Bellini in a 1–1 draw with [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]];<ref>{{cite web|url=http://forzaitalianfootball.com/2016/05/toni-and-bellini-a-tale-of-two-serie-a-farewell-penalties/|title=Toni And Bellini: A Tale of Two Serie A Farewell Penalties|publisher=forzaitalianfootball.com|date=10 May 2016|access-date=11 May 2016}}</ref> and on 14 May, [[Christian Abbiati]] for [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] in the last fixture of the season at home against [[A.S. Roma|Roma]], however, he did not get any playing time,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/84353/abbiati-goodbye-not-what-i-expected|title=Abbiati: 'Goodbye not what I expected'|publisher=Football Italia|date=14 May 2016|access-date=15 May 2016}}</ref> totaling 281 league appearances for the club.<ref name="Abbiati to retire">{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/84273/official-abbiati-retire|title=Official: Abbiati to retire|publisher=Football Italia|date=13 May 2016|access-date=13 May 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzettaworld.com/news/serie-a/milan/abbiati-set-to-retire/?refresh_ce-cp|title=AC Milan keeper readies for final San Siro bow|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|author1=Ogo Sylla|date=13 May 2016|access-date=13 May 2016}}</ref>
